notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 65-year-old female admitted for upper GI bleed. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.46, creatinine 0.68-0.74, hemoglobin 11.6-13.1, platelets 254-262, sodium 138-139, wbc 7.4-8; vitals dbp 68-73, heart_rate 69-73, map 87-89, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-16, sbp 120-127, spo2 97-98, temp 37-37.2
Day 0 orders/meds/results: EGD: bleeding duodenal ulcer, treated with endoscopic clips; Pantoprazole 80 mg IV
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Acute blood loss anemia.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient seen and examined at bedside. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.71-0.73, hemoglobin 10.2-11.2, platelets 254-265, sodium 138-139, wbc 7.3-7.8; vitals dbp 68-73, heart_rate 69-73, map 86-91, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-16, sbp 120-126, spo2 96-98, temp 36.9-37.2
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Transfuse 1 unit packed red blood cells
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Acute blood loss anemia. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 65-year-old female, length of stay 3 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Upper GI bleed. Acute blood loss anemia. Follow up with primary care in one week. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed.
